text:
sam_support: Escalation from customer AcmeCorp — internal ALB health checks started failing after a config push ~09:30 UTC. Instances in target group are marked Unhealthy, app returning 502s for a subset of pods behind Envoy. Customer is on Private VPC + transparent egress proxy (squid) on hosts. They report API errors for a single region only. Can we triage?

deploy-bot: (automated) deployed service/web@v2.3.8 to us-east-2 at 2026-08-17T09:27:45Z

ingrid_eng: Thanks — can you paste the ALB health check config and a short tcpdump from one of the affected targets? Also include `iptables-save -t nat` from the instance. My first suspicion: something is DNATing traffic (transparent proxy) and ALB health probe TCP->app is getting redirected to proxy which returns 503, so ALB marks unhealthy.

sam_support: Health check settings (from ALB TG): protocol=TCP, port=15001, interval=10s, timeout=6s, healthy threshold=2.
Attached tcpdump (snippet) and iptables as requested:

--- tcpdump -n -c 6 -w - tcpdump snippet ---
11:09:31.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54032 > 10.0.10.45.15001: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
11:09:31.123457 IP 10.0.10.45.15001 > 10.0.5.12.54032: Flags [S.], seq 3000, ack 12346, win 28960, length 0
11:09:31.123459 IP 10.0.10.45.15001 > 10.0.5.12.54032: Flags [R.], seq 3001, ack 12346, win 0, length 0
--- end snippet ---

iptables-save -t nat (relevant lines):
:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
-A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 80 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 3128
-A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 3129
COMMIT

sam_support: We *do* run a transparent proxy on hosts to enforce egress policies. The ALB health probe is TCP->15001 (Envoy) though — why would port 80/443 DNAT affect it?

rahul_net: That iptables snippet shows a broad PREROUTING DNAT for 80/443, but ALB probe is on 15001 — however I also see a last-minute network policy that uses nftables to rewrite ephemeral ports for traffic coming from 10.0.0.0/16; could be an interaction. Can you run this quick check on the instance: `sudo iptables -t nat -vnL PREROUTING --line-numbers` and `sudo tcpdump -n -i any tcp port 15001 and host 10.0.5.12`?

ingrid_eng: Another quick repro: from the instance, try `sudo socat -d -d TCP-LISTEN:15001,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:'/bin/cat'` and then `nc -vz 127.0.0.1 15001` to confirm local listener. If local accepts but ALB probe fails, suspect DNAT from PREROUTING rewriting destination to proxy on the host's NIC (packets hitting PREROUTING before local delivery). That explains the SYN->SYN-ACK then RST pattern if proxy upgrades/inspects and rejects.

rahul_net: I pulled the full `iptables-save -t nat` — there is an additional rule inserted by the egress-agent: `-A PREROUTING -p tcp -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j REDIRECT --to-ports 3128` (this grabs anything targeted at local ports on the host). ALB health probes to the host's local listener are matched by `--dst-type LOCAL` and get redirected to squid. So TCP handshake to 15001 gets handed to proxy, which doesn't speak plain TCP or PROXY protocol and responds with RST/503.

ingrid_eng: That matches the tcpdump: ALB SYN, host SYN-ACK (from envoy), then RST — proxy interfering mid-path. The fix is to add an explicit PREROUTING exception for the LB source CIDR or for the target port 15001 so the PREROUTING REDIRECT does not apply to ALB probe traffic. Example to insert above the generic rule: 

```
# skip transparent-redirect for ALB source range
sudo iptables -t nat -I PREROUTING 1 -s 10.0.5.0/24 -p tcp --dport 15001 -j ACCEPT
# or skip by destination port entirely
sudo iptables -t nat -I PREROUTING 1 -p tcp --dport 15001 -j RETURN
```
Note: use ACCEPT/RETURN depending on distribution/nft translation. Also update egress-agent config so rule persists across reboots/agent restarts.

sam_support: Can we apply this as a hotfix? Customer is seeing degraded traffic. We need a quick rollback plan if it breaks.

oncall_lead: OK to apply to the 3 affected hosts in the region during a 10-minute maintenance window. Add a smoke check after change: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>` and watch for states -> healthy within 2 intervals. If anything regresses, remove the new rule.

ingrid_eng: I've pushed a patch to the egress-agent config in staging and will roll to the 3 hosts now with a one-command change to insert the PREROUTING exception. Command used: `sudo iptables -t nat -I PREROUTING 1 -s 10.0.5.0/24 -p tcp --dport 15001 -j ACCEPT` then `sudo iptables -t nat -D PREROUTING 3` to keep order consistent with agent-managed chains.

sam_support: Applied to host-1/2/3. Waiting on health check.

ingrid_eng: ALB reports target health = healthy for all three hosts after ~30s. API 502s dropped to baseline. Asking egress-agent team to update default rule set to exclude known LB probe ports and add integration tests.

sam_support: Customer confirmed recovery. Marking this as resolved and adding runbook note. :white_check_mark:
